justification: Standard: second pass on the same class of bug as commit 50d0157e — source-control visibility and bootstrap-documentation accuracy, not production data or a served route. A silently-shadowed migration or fix script absent from a fresh clone is an operational gap, not a data-corruption risk, so Minor would understate it and Critical overstates it.

deferred_out_of_this_commit.why: 11 of the ~81 files this gitignore fix makes trackable also trip scripts/lint_hardcoded_zone_codes.py (DQ-30's guard against hardcoded NSW zone-code lists). Some read as legitimate (a Feb-2026 diagnostic verifying known DCP-documented zone values against DB state; heritage marker prefixes C1/C2/O1 that happen to collide with real zone-code shapes) and some read as genuine drift risk (migrations/create_housing_sepp_standards.py alone accounts for 36 of the 69 flags). Adjudicating each site and either adding a justified `# noqa: zone-codes` or wiring it to shared/zone-taxonomy.json is a real, separate review this reproducibility fix should not rush through or silently waive. Left untracked; still absent from a fresh clone.

falsifiable_check.command: git check-ignore -q scripts/definitions/import_definitions.py; test $? -eq 1; git check-ignore -q scripts/verification/check_heritage_duplication.py; test $? -eq 1
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Either file is still ignored, proving it would be absent from a fresh clone.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before this change: git check-ignore -v reported .gitignore:195 check_*.py / .gitignore:297 create_*.py for files under scripts/definitions, scripts/diagnostics, scripts/enrichment, scripts/fixes, scripts/procedural, scripts/verification, scripts/migrations, scripts/sql and the root migrations/ directory — the same basename-glob bug the prior commit fixed one directory level up, recurring one level deeper because `!scripts/*.py`-style negations don't cross `/`.
falsifiable_check.observed_green: git check-ignore -q now exits 1 (not ignored) for all files listed above; `git add -n` on the affected directories stages ~70 previously-invisible files with no unexpected inclusions (verified: __pycache__, backup JSON snapshots, bulk PDFs, and scripts/drawdown_creds.txt remain correctly excluded).

functions.name: load_definitions_from_json
functions.input: json_path (pathlib.Path) to a definitions JSON file
functions.output: list[dict] of definitions, or [] if the path does not exist
functions.if_none: Missing file prints a [SKIP] line and returns an empty list rather than raising; this script itself (and the scripts/definitions/extracted/*.json it reads) now exist in Git for a fresh clone to run at all, which is the defect this change fixes.

pre_impl.existing_data: None. This change only affects Git tracking and documentation text; it does not read or write database rows.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The prior commit's `!scripts/*.py` / `!scripts/*.sql` negations were assumed to cover the whole scripts/ tree; gitignore's `*` does not cross `/`, so they only reached files directly under scripts/, not scripts/<subdir>/.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Forward-only source-control repair, same as the prior commit. Existing working copies are unaffected; fresh clones now receive the previously-hidden files.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A — no external service called by the .gitignore/tracking change. The runbook's DeepSeek Harness install command and GitHub URL were verified via WebFetch against github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness directly (not secondary blog sources) before being left unchanged; the Node-version claim from third-party guides could NOT be confirmed against that primary source, so the runbook now says so explicitly rather than asserting an unverified number.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A — no frontend route or type touched.

break_it.scenario: A fresh Linux clone runs a DCP definitions or heritage-tagging fix script referenced in project docs (e.g. scripts/definitions/import_definitions.py, scripts/verification/check_heritage_duplication.py)
break_it.what_happens: python: can't open file — the script does not exist, because it was never committed.
break_it.how: .gitignore now re-includes *.py/*.sql/*.sh/*.mjs/*.js/*.bat at any depth under scripts/ (`!scripts/**/*.py` etc.), not just one level deep; all ~70 previously-shadowed files are now tracked.
break_it.repro: git ls-files scripts/definitions/ scripts/verification/ | wc -l  # was 0 for these two dirs before this change

break_it.scenario: An operator follows docs/LINUX_DEEPSEEK_BOOTSTRAP_RUNBOOK.md step 4 exactly as written before this change
break_it.what_happens: `git switch fix/linux-repro-gitignore-holes` fails — that branch was never pushed to origin, so the clone has no such ref, and the runbook's own 'staged but not yet committed' warning was already stale (the fix had in fact landed directly on main).
break_it.how: Runbook now states the repair is on main (no branch switch needed) and gives a git check-ignore command to verify both repair passes are present.
break_it.repro: git ls-remote --heads origin 'fix/linux-repro-gitignore-holes'  # empty, confirming the branch never existed on origin

break_it.scenario: Operator installs only the Node version this repo's SETUP.md specifies (20 LTS) and assumes it also satisfies DeepSeek Harness
break_it.what_happens: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` may fail to start if DSH's actual minimum (third-party guides claim ^22.19.0/>=24.x, unconfirmed by the DSH README itself) is higher than 20 LTS.
break_it.how: Runbook section 5 now flags the version as unconfirmed from DSH's primary source, tells the operator to read the actual startup error rather than trust a number, and to use nvm for a second Node version rather than replacing the repo's pinned one.
break_it.repro: n/a — documentation caveat, not a code path

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — a real fresh Linux clone + npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web run has not been performed (no Linux partition exists yet on the target machine); only Git visibility and primary-source documentation claims were verified from Windows.
